title: Dynamic Rule Orchestration for IoT Gateways
business: Industrial IoT gateway manufacturers who need to update device behavior without reflashing firmware.
problem: Hard-coded logic in C-based firmware prevents rapid adaptation to changing sensor data formats or new business rules, leading to costly maintenance cycles.
solution: Embedding the Lua interpreter allows developers to offload volatile business logic into lightweight scripts that the host application executes, enabling hot-swapping of device behavior.
steps: Integrate the Lua C API into the host firmware to initialize the virtual machine state.
Define a C-based interface that exposes specific sensor data structures to the Lua environment.
Load external Lua scripts containing device-specific processing logic into the interpreter.
Execute the Lua scripts during the main event loop to determine device actions based on input.
Use the Lua garbage collector to manage memory for script-defined tables and variables.
outcome: The gateway achieves modularity where logic updates occur via script deployment rather than full system recompilation, significantly reducing downtime.
limitation: Because Lua uses a register-based virtual machine, complex logic requiring heavy computational overhead can impact the host application's real-time constraints; monitor execution time per script cycle to ensure stability.
